what: Leak found by reading, which crates/hir-firewall (lane firewall) will report on its first run: `body_syntax(G)` in crates/hir-def/src/expr_store/body.rs is keyed by each body G and reads its file's parse and AstIdMap (via def_syntax / span_map / ast_id_map), so an edit of any one function body F re-executes body_syntax for EVERY other body of the same file (it backdates, but it is O(bodies in the file) per edit and breaks the guarantee that a body edit re-executes only F's queries; docs/v2/plan/lanes/firewall/notes.md section 3). Fix at the cause: a per-file query that gives each item's position-free syntax (or its hash and relative tree) as a field of a tracked struct per item, so body_syntax(G) reads only G's field and is not re-executed when another item's text changes, as the item tree's per-item keys already do (item_tree/items.rs, docs/v2/plan/lanes/frontend/reparse.md). Test: crates/hir-firewall/tests/exceptions.rs an_edit_of_each_function_reaches_only_it goes clean.
